decisions.reason: With row size 2 and threshold 1, column size 3 and threshold 3, and all points coincident, the pair is nonadmissible but the original larger-cardinality rule cannot select a nonleaf cluster. Added an explicit only-nonleaf branch; when both clusters are nonleaf, the original cardinality and row-tie rule remains. Each split still partitions the parent and descends one finite tree, so recursion terminates without choice.

Confirmed a nonfatal call-interface omission: the supplied dense m-by-n block already gives the exact admissible one-pair input (D,I_n), since D I_n*=D over both real and complex fields. Made this conversion explicit and stated the real/complex field, positive matrix size, integer cap, and nonnegative tolerances required by the called routine. This is a routine conversion, not an unsatisfied mathematical prerequisite. Effective cap min(k,m,n), zero blocks, exact diagonal/near copies, failure identity, and successful discarded-tail outputs are preserved.

The Example and both mathematical calculations are valid: self-distance is zero, threshold 2 makes both clusters leaves, and Eckart-Young applies to I_2 with k=1<dim(V)=2 and second singular value 1, so every rank-at-most-one B has spectral error at least 1. The final far-block label incorrectly describes this near block; replaced only that conclusion by the impossibility of replacing this dense near block at subunit error. This is a nonfatal terminology defect, with the rank obstruction and all hypotheses unchanged; diag(1,0) attains the endpoint error 1.
